title: Company Operations Blueprint: access, change, data, procurement, vendor lifecycle, and travel
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose
This blueprint consolidates company-wide procedures for access & permissions, change management, data stewardship, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, and travel. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and team leads to ensure consistent controls, minimize operational risk, and speed approvals across Redwood Inference.

Scope
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and consultants who request, approve, or operate systems or purchases on behalf of Redwood Inference. Exceptions require documented approval from Finance-Legal and Security.

Principles
- Least privilege by default for all system and data access.
- Separation of duties for procurement and vendor approvals.
- Risk-based controls: higher-sensitivity data/workflows require elevated review and monitoring.
- Observable, auditable change and procurement trails.
- Single source of truth for templates and forms; use the README at the top of each team folder.

1) Access and Permissions
Summary
Access requests must follow a documented lifecycle: request -> manager approval -> role owner approval -> periodic review. Access is granted for a specified TTL and reviewed at least quarterly.

Key roles and owners
- Requester: employee initiating request.
- Manager: approves business justification.
- Role Owner: team engineer or service owner who vets technical scope.
- IAM Admins: implement and revoke access (Security owns).

Standard process (for new service access)
1. Submit request via Access Request Form (internal link: /templates/access-request). Include justification, resource identifiers, and requested TTL.
2. Manager approval (manager must confirm business need).
3. Role Owner technical approval (defines minimal permissions).
4. Security (IAM Admin) creates role and issues time-bound credentials; credentials logged in Audit Log.
5. Auto-expiry: default TTL = 30 days for elevated access; 365 days for read-only data access unless higher sensitivity.

Approval thresholds and SSO groups
- Low-risk read-only to internal docs: manager only.
- Production system write access: manager + role owner + security (3-party).
- Admin-level or billing console: security and Finance-Legal review mandatory.

Periodic review and attestations
- Quarterly access review: team leads must attest to active users on their SSO groups.
- Orphaned accounts remediation: accounts with no activity for 90 days flagged for deprovision.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- Short-lived (max 4 hours) elevated keys issued by Security on-call with incident ticket. Must be logged and reviewed in post-incident.

2) Change Management
Summary
All changes that affect production services, infrastructure, or critical business processes must be tracked, reviewed, and — for high-risk changes — scheduled in the change calendar.

Change categories
- Standard changes: low-risk, pre-approved (routine deploys, dependency updates within validated ranges).
- Normal changes: require peer review and CI validation. Schedule to maintenance windows if impacting SLOs.
- Major changes: architecture, database migrations, or anything that may increase error budgets; require Change Advisory Board (CAB) signoff.

Process (normal and major changes)
1. Create a Change Request in the Change Registry (template: /templates/change-request). Include rollback plan, owner, test plan, and SLO impact estimate.
2. Peer review and automated validations (CI, staging smoke tests).
3. Schedule and notify stakeholders (72-hour minimum notice for major).
4. CAB review for major changes (members: Eng Platform lead, Security, SRE, Product manager, Finance-Legal for cost impact).
5. Execute with tracing enabled and automated rollback triggers.
6. Post-change review within 5 business days; update runbooks if necessary.

Risk controls and guardrails
- Database schema migrations must have backward-compatible read paths or a documented toggle to revert within 30 minutes.
- Rolling upgrades for cell-level services; avoid cluster-wide simultaneous reboots.
- Canary traffic minimum: 1% for 30 minutes or based on statistically significant sample of errors/latency.

3) Data Management and Classification
Summary
Data must be classified, stored, and processed according to sensitivity. This section defines classifications, retention, encryption, and access rules.

Classification tiers
- Public: intended for public consumption. No special handling.
- Internal: company-internal operational data (default). Stored in internal buckets with access control.
- Confidential: PII, customer prompts, model inputs tied to account identifiers. Encrypt at rest (KMS-managed) and restrict access to approved roles.
- Regulated: data subject to legal requirements (HIPAA, GDPR special categories). Requires Private deployment options and legal signoff.

Retention and deletion
- Default retention for Internal logs: 180 days.
- Confidential data: retention per contract; preserve for minimum compliance window then purge unless legal hold.
- Data deletion requests: routed to Data Steward and Legal; retention table and approved purge script required.

Storage and encryption
- All Confidential and Regulated data must be in customer-controlled KMS keys (when in Private deployments) or Redwood KMS with recorded key usage.
- Backups: encrypted and lifecycle-managed; test restores annually.

Data sharing and third parties
- Export of Confidential or Regulated data to vendors requires a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and security questionnaire completion. See Vendor Lifecycle below.

4) Procurement and Expense Controls
Summary
Procurement is centrally coordinated but delegated by thresholds. This section defines approvals, competitive sourcing, and expense submission norms.

Approval thresholds (USD)
- <$2,500: Requester’s manager approval.
- $2,500–$25,000: Manager + Finance representative. Competitive quotes recommended for >$10k.
- >$25,000: Formal procurement process: RFQ/RFP, legal review, and CFO approval.

Procurement steps (vendor/software/hardware)
1. Complete Procurement Request Form (/templates/procurement-request) with business case, budget code, and preferred supplier.
2. Procurement team validates budget and sourcing rules.
3. Security reviews for SaaS/infra (security questionnaire).
4. Contract by Legal and Finance signoff.
5. Purchase order issued; Finance records asset if CapEx.

Expense reimbursement and travel
- Use the Expenses app for employee reimbursements with itemized receipts.
- Per-diem and travel class: Economy for flights under 5 hours; Premium Economy or Business for flights >8 hours with Director+ approval. See Travel Policy below.

Non-standard spend (emergency/one-off)
- Emergency purchases must be recorded in Procurement log and retrospectively approved within 5 business days.

5) Vendor Lifecycle and Security Onboarding
Summary
Vendors are categorized by risk and onboarded through a standardized lifecycle: request -> security questionnaire -> contract -> provisioning -> periodic review.

Vendor risk categories
- Low: marketing tools, office supplies. Minimal security review.
- Medium: SaaS with customer data (analytics, billing). Requires security questionnaire and DPA.
- High: vendors with access to production systems or PII (hosting, backup, private inference nodes). Requires security assessment, annual audit rights, and executive sponsor.

Onboarding checklist
1. Capture vendor business case and owner.
2. Security questionnaire (must pass medium/high thresholds).
3. Legal: DPA & contract terms, SLA, liability caps.
4. Procurement: PO & payment terms.
5. Provisioning: least-privilege credentials, scoped service accounts, limited TTL tokens.
6. Monitoring: onboarding to vendor health dashboard and alerting if available.

Ongoing governance
- Annual vendor reviews for medium/high vendors.
- Access revocation when offboarding or contract termination with 14-day seed-to-zero account plan.

6) Travel Policy (business travel)
Summary
Travel should balance business needs, safety, and cost efficiency. All travel must be pre-approved in the Travel Request workflow.

Booking and approvals
- Domestic trips: Manager approval for trips <$2,000.
- Intl trips: Manager + People Ops approval for visa, insurance requirements.
- For multi-day conferences: conference budget must be pre-approved by Finance.

Class of travel
- Flights: Economy standard. Business class for flights >8 hours or for Director+ with justification.
- Hotels: mid-tier business hotels; policy allows upgrades with manager pre-approval.

Expense items
- Receipts required for meals, transport, lodging. Alcohol acceptable within reason and with itemized receipts.
- Per diem rates are set by region (see internal travel rates table: /templates/travel-rates).

Safety and incident reporting
- Register travel with People Ops for international travel.
- Any safety incidents must be reported within 24 hours to People Ops and Security.

7) Internal Templates and Forms (single source of truth)
All operational forms live under /templates. Teams must not store ad-hoc templates in team drives. Canonical templates include:
- access-request (Access Request Form)
- change-request (Change Registry entry)
- procurement-request (Procurement Request Form)
- vendor-security-questionnaire (Vendor Security Questionnaire)
- travel-request and travel-rates
- expense-reimbursement

8) Roles, Responsibilities, and RACI
High-level RACI (examples)
- Access provisioning: R=Requester, A=Manager, C=Role Owner, I=Security
- Procurement under $2.5k: R=Requester, A=Manager, C=Finance
- Major change: R=Service Owner, A=CAB, C=SRE/Security, I=Product/Finance

9) Auditability and Reporting
- All access grants, change requests, procurement records, and vendor contracts must be stored in the company audit system and retained per retention policy.
- Monthly operational dashboard: number of open change requests, overdue approvals (>7 days), orphaned users, high-risk vendors.

10) Exceptions and Waivers
- Exceptions to this blueprint require documented risk acceptance and signoff by Finance-Legal and Security. Temporary waivers must have TTL <= 30 days and an explicit mitigation plan.

11) Operational Playbook & Runbook Links
- For incident-driven emergency changes, refer to the Runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-deploy
- For quarterly access attestations: /confluence/people-ops/onboarding-and-offboarding

Appendix A — Quick checklists
Access request checklist:
- Business justification present
- Manager approval captured
- Role owner technical scope defined
- TTL specified

Procurement checklist (>$10k):
- Competitive quotes attached
- Security questionnaire completed
- Legal/Finance approvals present

Change request checklist:
- Rollback plan documented
- Canary traffic plan defined
- Post-change validation metrics specified

Appendix B — Glossary (short)
- Role Owner: technical owner of a service or dataset.
- CAB: Change Advisory Board.
- TTL: Time to Live (access expiration).
- DPA: Data Processing Addendum.

Change log
- 2024-11-15: Initial draft created by Ava Thompson.
- 2025-06-03: Added vendor risk categories and on-boarding checklist (reviewers: D. Park).
- 2026-02-20: Published with travel policy clarifications and retention updates.

Contact and ownership
Finance-Legal is the canonical owner of this blueprint. For questions or to request an exception, contact finance-legal@redwood.ai or submit via /support/ops-policy.
